results.title: Air Plan Approval; California; Revised Format for Materials Incorporated by Reference
results.abstract: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is revising the format for materials submitted by the State of California that are incorporated by reference into the California State Implementation Plan (SIP). The regulations and other materials affected by this format change have all been previously submitted by the State of California and approved by the EPA. This format revision will primarily affect the "Identification of plan--in part" sections, as well as the format of the SIP materials that will be available for public inspection at the EPA Regional Office and the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA). This action, which only relates to rules applicable within six California air districts, is the fifth and final of a series of actions intended to change the format for the entire California SIP.

results.title: Air Plan Revisions; Arizona; Maricopa County Air Quality Department; New Source Review; Emission Reduction Credits
results.abstract: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is taking final action to approve a revision to the Maricopa County Air Quality Department (MCAQD or "Department") portion of the Arizona State Implementation Plan (SIP). This revision establishes a federally enforceable program allowing for the generation of emission reduction credits (ERCs) by retrofitting or replacing existing on-road vehicles with lower emitting vehicles while meeting other Clean Air Act (CAA or "Act") requirements. These ERCs are intended to be used as offsets for major stationary sources under the Department's Nonattainment New Source Review (NNSR) program. The EPA is approving this SIP revision because we find that it meets the applicable CAA requirements.

results.title: Air Quality Implementation Plans; California; San Joaquin Valley; 2015 8-Hour Ozone Nonattainment Area Requirements; and California Consumer Products Regulations
results.abstract: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) proposes to approve State implementation plan (SIP) revisions submitted by the State of California to meet Clean Air Act (CAA or "Act") requirements for the 2015 8-hour ozone national ambient air quality standards (NAAQS or "standards") in the San Joaquin Valley ozone nonattainment area ("San Joaquin Valley" or "SJV"). In this document, the EPA refers to these submissions collectively as the "SJV 70 ppb Ozone SIP." The EPA proposes to approve the SJV 70 parts per billion (ppb) Ozone SIP as meeting the applicable ozone nonattainment area requirements for emissions inventories, reasonably available control measures, attainment demonstration, rate of progress and reasonable further progress, motor vehicle emissions budgets, and enhanced monitoring. The EPA is also initiating the adequacy process for the budgets included in this SIP submission through this proposed rule. The EPA also proposes to approve two SIP revisions amending the SIP to incorporate changes reflecting updates to California Air Resources Board (CARB) Consumer Products Regulations and Method 310, which apply statewide and upon which the SJV 70 ppb Ozone SIP relies. These regulations concern emissions of volatile organic compounds (VOC) from antiperspirants, deodorants, consumer products, and aerosol coating products, and Method 310 is used to determine the VOC and reactive organic compounds content of these products. The EPA proposes to approve these regulations for purposes of the State's SIP under the CAA.
